svg.title: One grid, three windows
svg.desc: A layered map is one square grid of 128 by 128 cells, each 16 pixels square. Each of its three layers is a rectangle cut from that grid, and the map's header says where each rectangle starts. In Goma Cave's entrance room the ground layer starts at cell 0, 0 and holds the cave floor and its pool; the middle layer starts at cell 0, 34, below it, and holds the rock walls; the overhead layer starts at cell 50, 0, to the right, and holds only the glow of the torches. The rest of the grid is unused.
svg.text: from cell 0, 0: the floor, at the back
from cell 50, 0: torch glow, in front
The map's header says where each window starts.
